articles.title: Cruz Montana's Surprise WWE Debut Shows What's Right and Wrong With NXT's Pipeline
articles.summary: Cruz Montana made his main roster debut Monday night on WWE Raw, revealing himself to be the latest member of The 946 and joining the faction in a beatdown of Roman Reigns and The Bloodline.
articles.body:
Cruz Montana made his main roster debut Monday night on WWE Raw, revealing himself to be the latest member of The 946 and joining the faction in a beatdown of Roman Reigns and The Bloodline.

It was a momentous occasion, one that has been long overdue for the veteran competitor, and the culmination of a career-long journey to the brightest lights and the biggest stage.

While Montana's promotion is welcome, his sudden arrival on Raw highlights both the strengths and weaknesses of WWE's pipeline from NXT to the main roster.

The days of Superstars overstaying their time in developmental are (mostly) over.

There will always be some who stick around the NXT locker room longer than others, thanks in large part to a television contract and the need to keep at least some recognizable names on the show.

Still, the Raw and SmackDown creative teams are more willing to call up a young star on little notice today than they have been in the past. It has led to some much-needed roster rejuvenation, too.

Since the beginning of 2026, we have witnessed Oba Femi, Joe Hendry, Trick Williams, Sol Ruca, Blake Monroe, Ricky Saints, Fatal Influence, Jaida Parker, OTM, Lola Vice, Tatum Paxley, and "All Ego" Ethan Page make the jump to the main roster.

For the most part, they have received significant television time and helped freshen up Raw and SmackDown from an in-ring perspective.

More importantly, it gives the talent the opportunity to sink or swim, rather than holding them off television for too long or delaying a call-up. Williams is one instance of a Superstar who was in NXT a touch too long. Luckily, he maintained his popularity, and the fans greeted his arrival with open arms.

He is a rare exception in this new landscape, where talents deemed "ready" are quickly thrust into the spotlight. Some in significant spots.

Williams quickly won the United States Championship. Jacy Jayne won the women's equivalent. Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid captured the Women's Tag Team Championships. Montana, Parker, Bronco Nima, and Lucien Price are embroiled in a main event rivalry with The Bloodline that will likely culminate in a Survivor Series: War Games main event.

Then there is Femi, who is tapped as the next big thing in WWE following a series against Brock Lesnar in which he retired The Beast after a convincing Hell in a Cell victory.

The pipeline from NXT to the main roster has fueled a youth movement within WWE, which was necessary as the median age of on-screen performers rose. It has also freshened things up and given performers the chance to prove they belong early on while getting reps on live television every Monday and Friday night.

As beneficial as it has been to the wrestlers and the product, there is also a fairly significant negative that should be addressed.

There is such a thing as having too much talent.

While an influx of new stars and fresh TV rivalries is important for the product's long-term sustainability, calling wrestlers up without any defined role is problematic.

It creates a logjam of Superstars, where there are plenty of talented performers worthy of the opportunity, but only so many spots to fill. The result is talent that is left off the show, out of the public eye, and withering away in irrelevance when they could have remained in NXT and at least worked with the next generation of stars to come up on that show.

It leaves the wrestler feeling disillusioned, and the audience loses track of them and ultimately stops caring.

One great example is Ilja Dragunov, who was the United States champion at one point before fading into the background and then off television, before leaving the company for more opportunities in All Elite Wrestling.

We have seen Saints arrive on SmackDown, have a few important matches here and there, then disappear for chunks of time. Ditto Carmelo Hayes, who inexplicably found himself off television post-WrestleMania 42, despite delivering bangers and reigning as the United States champion.

Giulia is another great example of a talent with all the tools needed to be a star, who was called up, given little to do despite two reigns as women's United States champion, and she is still struggling to find her footing on the main roster as a result.

Yes, not letting talent wallow in NXT when they are ready for bigger and better is great, but introducing them with pomp and circumstance, then not having anything for them creatively is worse than the alternative.

What comes next for The 946 after their inevitable loss to The Bloodline in this marquee rivalry? WWE should already have a plan for this talented faction—all but one of its members are NXT call-ups—rather than waiting until the feud ends to figure out how to use them.

Some will return to NXT and establish themselves as legitimate main event stars, a la Grayson Waller, but others will stay in the background before being released or forgotten for the remainder of their contracts.

That is when it becomes an indictment of the creative team, exposing the downside of calling up so much NXT talent without a clear plan.

articles.title: 'No Excuse,' Canadiens' Cole Caufield Rips Historic 4-Goal Collapse vs. Jets, 'It's Terrible'
articles.summary: Montreal Canadiens forward Cole Caufield didn't hold back when discussing his team's shocking meltdown in a 5-4 overtime home loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Montreal Canadiens forward Cole Caufield didn't hold back when discussing his team's shocking meltdown in a 5-4 overtime home loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night.

Speaking to reporters after the Habs squandered a four-goal lead in the third period, Caufield said, "Guys thought the game was over. We had a four-goal lead. There's no excuse for this. It's terrible."

Caufield scored two of the Canadiens' four goals, and they appeared to be cruising toward an easy victory.

Report Card Grades for Every Team's 1st Month 🔠

Montreal led 4-0 with less than three minutes remaining in regulation, but the Jets inexplicably scored four goals in just over two minutes of game time to tie it.

After goals by Tyrel Bauer and Morgan Barron at 17:21 and 18:03 of the third period, star winger Kyle Connor scored two goals 27 seconds apart to tie the game with just 33 seconds remaining.

That sent the game into overtime where defenseman Dylan Samberg scored 3:30 into the extra session to complete the unbelievable comeback.

Per ESPN's Greg Wyshynski , it marked the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history, starting at 57:21, which broke the previous record by nearly five minutes.

The loss ended a five-game winning streak for Montreal, although it did still manage to get a point for the eighth consecutive game.

Losing in that fashion can be demoralizing for a team, though, making it of the utmost for the Habs to bounce back in their next game against the Utah Mammoth on Thursday.

Nobody is doubting that the Ducks' young core has a bright future. We've seen it shine offensively and on the power play through the first month of this season. But their defense just isn't even close to where it needs to be, as they sit near the bottom of the league, allowing nearly four goals (3.80) per game. They're fun to watch between their high-scoring affairs and all the Gauthier hat tricks, but they'll have to learn this season that there's another end of the ice.

Needing a second hat trick in two games out of Gauthier to beat the Canucks 5-4 isn't exactly a recipe for longevity.

If the Bruins hadn't yet convinced you of their legitimacy, Monday's 3-2 win over the Golden Knights should've done the trick.

Whether you saw them coming this year or not, they are sitting firmly atop the Atlantic with their 11-4-1 record and plus-20 goal differential, and the full team keeps passing the necessary tests. Captain David Pastrňák has eight goals and 20 points in 16 games, rookie James Hagens put together a Calder Trophy-worthy first month, and both Jeremy Swayman and Michael DiPietro look fantastic in net.

The Sabres have been turning things around lately with three straight wins, but even then it's going to take more work for them to climb out of their 7-4-3 hole. Goaltending remains an issue, as Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen had just one game over .900 in his last five starts, and backup Colten Ellis is unpredictable.

Losing the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes stings, as do all of the offseason departures that gave this roster a little more meat. We'll see if the Sabres keep gaining traction and start eyeing the trade market.

Report Card Grades for Every Team's 1st Month 🔠

Don't look now, but the Flames have climbed out of their terrible start with a 7-3-0 record in their last 10. It's not like they're going to make some elaborate playoff run now — that was never the goal — but the fight they're showing now is a good sign for the future.

They own the fifth-best power play in the league with a 30.6 percent success rate, and Devin Cooley has been giving Dustin Wolf some help in a down year.

The Hurricanes are 12-3-2 and leading the NHL in standings points one month into the season. They look poised to go back-to-back, not just because of the early success, but because of how they're doing it.

Pyotr Kochetkov is looking like he's arrived, setting a franchise record with a 10-game winning streak to start the 2026–27 season. According to MoneyPuck.com , he ranks third among netminders league-wide with 9 goals saved above expected. The Hurricanes as a whole are No. 2, averaging just 2.29 goals against per game.

On the offensive side, they're No. 3 league-wide with a 3.76 goals-per-game average. Jackson Blake has continued to grow on his post-season magic with a point-per-game average; Sebastian Aho has had a great start to the season with nine goals and 21 points in 17 games; and the best-oiled machine in the league is looking near-perfect.

If you thought 2026 Patrick Kane was going to be the answer to Connor Bedard's winger prayers, it appears you were wrong. Kane's got just one goal, a team-worst -15 rating, and 14 penalty minutes in 15 games as the Blackhawks continue to struggle. What's worse: the future Hall of Famer is going to be sidelined with an upper-body injury.

There's only so much we can expect out of 37-year-old Kane, but showtime is looking more like a curtain call this season in Chicago.

Should the Avalanche panic at this point? Not exactly. They're still tied with Dallas for third in the Central, and they've got enough wiggle room and star power to rise above this rocky period. But it's certainly a rocky period for the Avalanche, as they've gone 5-4-1 in their past 10, and a 7-2 loss to the flailing Blue Jackets is exactly what you don't want to see in that situation.

Don't let a big win over the Avalanche distract you from the fact that the Blue Jackets are 6-7-0 with a -12 goal differential and struggling to score. The 7-2 win Tuesday could be the gateway to unlocking some of the offensive power this team is sorely lacking, but the lack of Kirill Marchenko on this roster is palpable.

Things haven't been perfect for the Stars to start the season, and that's shown in the standings as the Mammoth and Wild have gone back and forth with the first two Central spots for most of October and early November.

But we're starting to see the consistency we all know from Dallas peak out again. The team is 7-3-0 in its last 10 games and third league-wide, averaging just 2.33 goals against. Maybe Tuesday's six-goal explosion and Jason Robertson's hat trick are an indication that better days are to come offensively.

If you're living under a rock, former Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin is now sitting out of the Red Wings lineup until his trade request is honored. The Red Wings haven't played too shabby in the meantime: They're 6-2-2 in their last 10, an improvement on the beginning of the season.

Their recent upswing is just another reminder that they'll be better off when this limbo ends, and everyone can move on.

With nine goals and 31 assists for 40 points in 16 games, Connor McDavid isn't just leading the league in points by 11 -- he has more assists than anyone else has points.

Guess who's 11 points behind him for No. 2 in scoring? Teammate Leon Draisaitl, with 13 goals and 29 points in 16 games. No. 3, you ask? Evan Bouchard, who is leading all defensemen with 28 points in 16 games.

There was concern that Mike Babcock coming in as head coach might've made the Oilers reinvent the wheel and stray from the high-scoring game they're known for, but instead, so far, they've managed a whole new level of scoring. It's working, as they're leading the Pacific with an 11-2-3 record and a +19 goal differential.

The Panthers have started to figure it out after a sloppy start to the season. They haven't been perfect, but their defense is stepping up even with Aleksander Barkov and Jacob Markstrom currently out with injuries.

While their usual league-best depth scoring is struggling to get chances right now, the overall clean defense and top-10 PK percentage are signs that the Panthers could bounce back and go on a decent run later on in the season.

Look, it's not polite to drag someone for their age, and we don't mean to keep ragging on the Kings for their aging roster. But it's no individual player's fault that GM Ken Holland chose to sign as many veterans as he did, and the team as a whole has suffered for it.

The team has needed oomph and some youthful quickness to get past the first round. Management went in the opposite direction in the offseason, and now it's looking like the Kings won't even make it to their yearly first-round exit.

As the season keeps trudging along, the Wild are looking more and more legit. They've climbed to the top of the Central thanks to some epic performances that just won't slow down. Kirill Kaprizov is nearly netting a goal per game for 26 points in 17 games overall; meanwhile, Matt Boldy is heading up with two goals and six points in his last five games.

They're pulling away with control over the Central, and it's deserved.

Flukey collapse to the Jets aside, the Canadiens are doing exactly what they need to be doing after an inconsistent start. Jacob Fowler is emerging as a Calder Trophy candidate in net and is giving the Habs the goaltending they need as things stabilize. According to MoneyPuck.com, he's second among all NHL goaltenders with 9.8 goals saved above expected.

The Predators are the best of the bad Central teams

The Devils just feel inevitable right now as they continue their ascent in their second week with Connor Hellebuyck in net.

They're 8-2-0 in their last ten and second in the Metro behind the immovable object that is the Hurricanes. They're receiving production from everywhere; they're playing a sound defensive game, and now they're getting world-class goaltending. Watch out, world.

The Islanders are playing some very defensively sound hockey right now, which is a step in the right direction under head coach Pete DeBoer. They'll take it for now, and they're hovering around a playoff spot, but they're going to need to build on this offensively if they're to make a meaningful playoff run. Could they scour the trade market for some scoring help for Matthew Schaefer?

Losing Igor Shesterkin to a devastating knee injury at the beginning of a season that felt promising for the Rangers stunk, but it's just the reality of the situation. And that reality shows that it's extremely difficult for a team that's going through changes and looking for a new identity to survive without its world-class goaltender.

The Rangers are still in the middle of the pack in the Metro due to their hot start, but they're trending down, and you can't blame them given the circumstances.

The Senators started out the season atop the Atlantic, but they've been a bit shaky recently — especially after the loss of William Eklund. Tim Stützle's emergence has been a treat, and he's chipped in nine goals and 21 points in 16 games to show his team that life will go on after Brady Tkachuk. Beyond the first two lines, though, the Senators are going to need more production to get back on a consistent track.

Had to pull out the thesaurus to describe just how unequipped these young Flyers are to return to the playoffs. Their brutal start to the season has culminated in the worst goal differential in the East (-21). They're mostly struggling to score at a league-worst 2.18 goals per game.

The Penguins aren't total garbage, but there's nothing particularly inspiring coming out of Pittsburgh this season. They're in a three-way tie for last in the Metro with a 5-8-2 record and a -3 goal differential, and the wheels appear to be falling off amid this three-game losing streak. They just don't seem to have it in what was supposed to be the last hurrah for the elders.

This hasn't been the start the Sharks wanted, with a 7-8-1 record and a -12 goal differential. Macklin Celebrini is only one person, and he can only do so much; the rest of the roster needs to be able to at least generate some chances while he's not on the ice.

This team just may not be ready yet for its first playoff appearance in the Celebrini era, unless the depth players figure it out and the defense tightens up.

The Kraken are in a decent spot with an 8-5-1 record sitting in a Wild Card spot out West. "Decent" is exactly how it feels, and their goal differential of precisely zero tells that story.

They are allowing a whopping 3.71 goals per game, which is bottom-five league-wide. They're also scoring 3.57 goals per game. It's pretty much all coming out in the wash. The good news? It's a clean page for newcomer Matthew Wood to paint some goals on.

The bad news? It's yet another year in which we're waiting for a Kraken player to make a splash and make us less confused about the direction of the team in the process.

The St. Louis Blues are 5-5-0 in their last 10 with a goal differential of 0 as they sit at third-worst in the Central. All is par for the course for the most underwhelming hockey team of the mid-to-late 2020s.

All should be well in theory for the Lightning: They're third and in a playoff spot in the brutal Atlantic, and they're scoring at the fourth-highest clip in the NHL with 3.71 goals per game.

Star and reigning Hart Trophy winner Nikita Kucherov apparently isn't satisfied with the way his contract talks are going. His early-season trade request makes things awkward as the Lightning look poised for the playoffs, even if he still intends to play.

Are the Leafs back to their old selves? Auston Matthews is sure looking like it, with 11 goals and 26 points in 17 games. The offense as a whole is, too, sitting at No. 5 league-wide, averaging 3.65 goals per game.

The Atlantic is so tough that they're 8-7-2 and just one point away from last in the division, but things are at least looking a bit more hopeful in Toronto right now.

The Mammoth (10-6-0) have managed to hold their own in the Central, hovering over the beasts like the Avalanche and the Stars for most of the season.

They've got some work to do, and you wonder if they're going to seek a new goaltending direction at the trade deadline. But it's exciting to see them thrive in the most top-heavy division in the league.

The Canucks are just as bad as everyone anticipated, sitting in the basement of the Pacific with the worst goal differential in the league. They're letting in 4.5 goals per game, far and away the worst goals-against average in the NHL.

With Elias Pettersson enjoying a bit of a bounce-back, though, could they trade him and look towards the future?

The Golden Knights have had an alright start to the season that just hasn't been much to write home about for last season's Cup losers. They've never quite had to put the foot on the gas early to find success later on in the season, so there's no real concern here. But the Oilers sure look better than ever, so it could end up backfiring.

The Capitals have hovered around the middle of the Metropolitan Division and are staying in the playoff conversation to start the season, but something just feels off game by game. They're struggling against top opponents like the Wild and the Stars.

Maybe the lack of oomph is in Alex Ovechkin's performance: He's got just one goal in 14 games to start his last NHL season.

Whether they're being forced to trade their Vezina and Hart Trophy-winning goaltender or losing nine games in a row, the Winnipeg Jets are going to be in your newsfeed nearly every day this season.

The latest? Less than three minutes away from suffering a 10-game winless streak at the hands of Montreal on Tuesday, they scored a franchise record-setting four goals over a 126-second span to force overtime, where Dylan Samberg delivered the winner to seal it 5-4.

articles.title: Ice hockey federation reiterates opposition to reinstatement of Russia
articles.summary: The CAS ruled last week to overturn governing body’s exclusion of ‌Russia over its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
articles.body:
The International ‌Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has said it ⁠maintains its ⁠disagreement with a Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision to reinstate Russian teams, warning of “significant ⁠practical and sporting challenges”.

The statement on Wednesday follows announcements from Norway, Denmark, Sweden and the Czech Republic that ⁠their national teams will refuse to play against Russia at next year’s men’s World Championships in Germany.

The CAS ruled last week to overturn the governing body’s exclusion of ‌Russia from international competition following its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

“As presented to the CAS, the immediate reintegration of Russian teams presents significant practical and sporting challenges, including visa and entry requirements, security provisions, logistical constraints and consequences for competition formats,” ⁠the IIHF said.

The decision has prompted ⁠widespread backlash. Latvia and Finland have also said their teams will not play Russia, while the Finnish city of Turku threatened to ⁠drop hosting duties for the 2028 World Junior Championship.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark ⁠Carney said Russia and Belarus ⁠will be barred from the upcoming World Junior Championship in Alberta. Moscow criticised the move, with Russian ambassador Oleg Stepanov telling state-run news agency TASS that Canada was “bringing politics even into junior hockey”.

The IIHF said it remains in dialogue with ‌national ‌associations, host authorities and organisers to determine the best path forward.

Skoda would ‘reassess’ sponsorship if Russia reinstated

Czech carmaker Skoda Auto, the main sponsor of the ice hockey world championships, said on Wednesday it would “reassess” its sponsorship if Russia takes part in the annual tournament.

“If the Russian national team takes part in the tournament, we will reassess our involvement in the tournament and take further action,” Skoda told the AFP news agency in a statement.

It added that Russia’s return to the tournament was “incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld”.

Skoda Auto, a unit of Germany’s Volkswagen, has been the tournament’s official main sponsor since 1993. It also sponsors the Tour de France.

Its spokeswoman Ivana Povolna refused to specify the amount Skoda spends on the ice hockey world championships annually.

Skoda’s annual report for 2025 says the company lent 45 electric cars to the organisers, while its designers made the crystal trophy for the most valuable player of the tournament.

articles.title: Sean Payton's success was the exception, not the rule, for Saints
articles.summary: We don't know if Kellen Moore can build a winner, but history shows his Saints predecessor Sean Payton's success was the exception, not the rule.
articles.body:
Fans of the New Orleans Saints witnessed their former coach Sean Payton lead the Denver Broncos to a 6-2 record on Sunday, putting him at 200 career wins in his NFL coaching career. The Broncos pulled out a 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs with 15 unanswered fourth quarter points and a last second goal-line stand for their fourth win in a row. Meanwhile, the 2-5 Saints were on a bye after losing their fourth out of five games last Sunday in Paris. Making matters perhaps more bitter for New Orleans fans was the fact that former Saints defensive lineman Malcolm Roach made the game-saving play for the Broncos with a fourth-down sack on Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

Sean Payton was the head coach of the Saints from 2006 to 2020. In 15 years on the sidelines, he owned a 152-89 regular season record with nine playoff appearances, eight division titles, three conference title game trips, and a Super Bowl XLIV championship. Since becoming coach of the Broncos in 2023, Payton has a 58-37 regular season record with two trips to the playoffs and a division title along with an appearance in last year's AFC Championship Game.

Payton walked away from the Saints, resigning after the 2021 regular season. After a year away from coaching, New Orleans traded his rights to the Denver Broncos. In exchange, the Saints got a 2023 first round draft choice, Bryan Bresee, and a 2024 second round draft choice, eventually swapped for Kool-Aid McKinstry. Bresee is out for the season with a knee injury and McKinstry has struggled at times. Generally though, both are good players and important to the defense.

It isn't what the Saints got for Payton that should anger fans. The fact that their former coach has done so well somewhere else while New Orleans has floundered is particularly galling. In their sixth year since Payton the Saints have a 29-46 record, a winning percentage of .387. Dennis Allen was the first choice to replace Payton. That failed miserably, with Allen bumbling to an 18-25 record from 2022 before being fired nine games into the 2024 season. Next up was Kellen Moore, hired in 2025 for his first ever head coaching job. In Moore, the Saints thought they were getting another offensive-minded coach for their rebuild. Through nearly a season and a half, that has most decidedly not been the case.

Moore's teams are 8-16 so far, with a winning percentage of .333 worse than Dennis Allen's results (10-14) through the same stretch of his tenure. Expected to be a much-improved team on offense in Moore's second year, the Saints instead are incapable of running the ball or protecting quarterback Tyler Shough with one of the most ill-prepared weekly game plans in the league. As a result, Kellen Moore is considered on the hot seat, with most fans expecting (hoping?) he doesn't last this entire season. If/when the Saints do move on from Moore, then it's back to the coaching drawing board. Don't assume that New Orleans will get it right. More often than not historically, they have not.

Only two of the twelve head coaching hires in the Saints 60-year history have a winning record. Sean Payton and Jim Mora were those two. Mora owned a 93-74 record (.557) and four playoff appearances in eleven years with the franchise without a postseason win. Payton, Mora, Jim Haslett (10-6 in 2000), and Dennis Allen (9-8 in 2023) were the only ones who pulled off a winning season, with just Haslett outside of Payton and Mora taking the Saints to the playoffs. Of the other eight coaches, only Bum Phillips and Dick Nolan even had one year of .500 football. That's simply not a good track record.

Kellen Moore would seem to need a monumental turnaround to keep his job with the Saints beyond this season. Irony being as cruel as it is, Saints fans witnessed Payton record his 200th career regular season victory last Sunday with another franchise. That and Moore's current struggles only highlight the historic futility New Orleans has had on the sidelines, making one a skeptic if the next choice will be the right one.

articles.title: John Hunter Nemechek To Drive HFT’s No. 41 O’Reilly Series Entry in 2027
articles.summary: After an unceremonious exit from LEGACY MOTOR CLUB’s NASCAR Cup Series program, John Hunter Nemechek has landed on his feet. The 29-year-old racer will join...
articles.body:
After an unceremonious exit from LEGACY MOTOR CLUB's NASCAR Cup Series program , John Hunter Nemechek has landed on his feet. The 29-year-old racer will join Haas Factory Team in 2027 and will pilot the organization's No. 41 Chevrolet in a full-time NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series campaign.

Nemechek, who will replace the departing Sam Mayer as the driver of the car, will have Jason Trinchere as his crew chief at HFT. Pye-Barker Fire & Safety, Nemechek's longtime sponsorship partner, will move with him to Haas Factory Team next season.

Nemechek, an 11-time race winner in NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series competition, is happy to see what he can do with Haas Factory Team, an organization that has fielded two strong championship-caliber entries in 2026.

"I'm excited to join Haas Factory Team's O'Reilly Auto Parts Series program," Nemechek said in a team press release. "They have championship-caliber cars and personnel, and I'm ready to get to work with this group and compete for wins in 2027."

With Mayer and Sheldon Creed, who had three wins in 2026, moving on at season's end , Haas Factory Team had to find a driver capable of winning races at the O'Reilly Series level to fill the void. With Nemechek becoming available as LEGACY MOTOR CLUB goes in a different direction in 2027, HFT saw an amazing opportunity with JHN.

"John Hunter brings the experience and talent we're looking for at Haas Factory Team," said Joe Custer, President of Haas Factory Team. "We're excited to have him join our organization and look forward to competing for wins and championships together."

As Haas Factory Team expands to three full-time entries in 2027, Nemechek will join Dean Thompson, who was previously announced to the 2027 driver roster for HFT , and another driver to be announced later.

In addition to his 11 career wins in the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, Nemechek is also a 13-time race winner in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series. While his record in the other two NASCAR National Series ranks hasn't translated to NASCAR Cup Series success, Nemechek should be seen as a championship contender in 2027.

articles.title: Florida high school football playoffs: Dates, brackets, schedule
articles.summary: Florida's 2026 high school football playoff brackets arrive Nov. 6. Here's the FHSAA postseason schedule, new Open Division and championship locations.
articles.body:
The road to a state championship is almost here for Florida high school football teams .

The Florida High School Athletic Association (FHSAA) is set to release its 2026 football playoff brackets this week, giving teams across the state their postseason matchups and a clearer picture of what it will take to reach a state championship.

The postseason officially begins later this month, with regional quarterfinals in the traditional state championship series. The newly introduced eight-team Open Division also begins pool play that weekend.

Here's everything to know about the 2026 Florida high school football playoffs, including when brackets are released, the postseason schedule and where the state championships will be played.

When are brackets for the Florida high school football playoffs released?

The FHSAA will release its 2026 high school football playoff brackets Friday, Nov. 6, at 5 p.m. ET.

The announcement will reveal the playoff qualifiers, seeds and first-round matchups for the upcoming postseason. Teams will learn their paths toward a state championship as the brackets are unveiled.

When do high school football playoffs start in Florida?

The 2026 FHSAA high school football playoffs begin Friday, Nov. 13, with some games likely set to begin on Thursday, Nov. 12.

The traditional state championship series will follow this schedule:

The eight-team Open Division will begin pool play Friday, Nov. 13, with additional games scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20 and Friday, Nov. 27. The Open Division semifinals are scheduled for Saturday, Dec. 5.

How to watch the Florida high school football playoffs

Fans can stream the Florida high school football postseason on the NFHS Network .

Where are the state championships located?

The 2026 FHSAA state championship games will be played at South Dade Kia Field at Pitbull Stadium on the campus of Florida International University in Miami.

The venue will host the championship games for Classes 1A-6A and the Open Division during championship week, Dec. 9-12.

The Range at H.G. Morse Stadium in Sumterville will host the Open Division semifinals, along with the Independent League and Florida Invitational Tournament championships.

articles.title: Bhayshul Tuten injury update: Latest on Jaguars' running back
articles.summary: Liam Coen provided an injury update on Jacksonville Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten ahead of Thursday's game with the Ravens.
articles.body:
The status of Jacksonville Jaguars' RB Bhayshul Tuten in Thursday's matchup with the Baltimore Ravens is up in the air at this time.

The good news is that after Tuten missed the last two days of practice with ankle and foot injuries, head coach Liam Coen said that he expects him to do "something" on Wednesday, according to Mia O'Brien.

Tuten told Coen that he feels better as of Wednesday.

However, when it comes to Tuten's availability against the Ravens, he will be a game-time decision.

Tuten has been quite good this season, averaging 4.5 yards per carry while scoring three touchdowns. With his speed, Tuten has proven to be very difficult to bring down. In the passing game, he has 15 receptions for 181 yards and three more touchdowns.

He is coming off a career game against the Colts , where Tuten rushed for over 100 yards and added another 55 yards to his overall total through the air. Tuten scored two touchdowns as well.

If he can't go or is on a snap count, the Jaguars will turn to Chris Rodriguez, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah providing depth.

articles.title: Youth Olympics: Tanvi Patri creates history, becomes first Indian woman to reach badminton semifinals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's rising badminton star Tanvi Patri scripted history at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on Wednesday, becoming the first Indian woman to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's rising badminton star Tanvi Patri scripted history at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on Wednesday, becoming the first Indian woman to reach the semifinals of the badminton competition.The 15-year-old from Odisha achieved the milestone with an impressive straight-game victory over Thailand's seventh seed Kakanik Kungkaew in the women's singles quarterfinals. Third seed Tanvi prevailed 21-17, 21-13 in 39 minutes to book her place in the last four.With the win, Tanvi joined an exclusive group of Indian shuttlers to have reached the badminton semifinals at the Youth Olympics. However, she is the first woman from the country to achieve the feat.Only three Indian players had previously reached this stage. HS Prannoy won silver at the inaugural Youth Olympics in Singapore in 2010, while Lakshya Sen also finished runner-up at the 2018 edition in Buenos Aires. Aditya Joshi reached the boys' singles semifinals in 2014 but returned without a medal.Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe next in Tanvi's wayTanvi, who trains at the Centre for Excellence in Bengaluru, will face Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe in the semifinal. The Indian youngster will be looking to settle an old score against her Japanese opponent, having lost their only previous meeting at the 2024 Pathum Thani Junior International Series in Thailand. Watanabe won that encounter 21-14, 21-10.A victory in the semifinal would guarantee Tanvi at least a silver medal and make her the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Youth Olympics. Even if she loses in the last four, she will have another opportunity to fight for bronze.Tanvi had earlier topped Women's Singles Group F with three successive victories to qualify for the knockout stage. In her final group match, she defeated Australia's Smrithi Adepu 21-4, 21-12 in a winner-takes-all contest.Another milestone in a promising careerThe Youth Olympics breakthrough adds to Tanvi's growing list of achievements. Earlier, she won the girls' singles U-17 title at the Badminton Asia U-17 and U-15 Championships in Chengdu, China, after defeating compatriot in an all-Indian final.With that triumph, she became the first Indian shuttler to win both the continental U-15 and U-17 titles.Now, the Odisha teenager has another opportunity to make history in Dakar. articles.title: Oliver Solberg relishing Toyota’s historic Celica WRC revival for 2027
articles.summary: The World Rally Championship runner-up reflects on 2026 title defeat and chance to be part of Celica history in next year
articles.body:
Oliver Solberg reckons it is "awesome" to be part of the revival of the iconic Toyota Celica brand in the World Rally Championship - and is ready to move on from this year's title heartbreak.

A little over a month since Solberg saw his dream to become world champion end two corners from the finish of the final stage, the Swede was named as one of three drivers that will pilot the all-new factory Toyota GR Celica Rally1 car next year.

Toyota announced on Tuesday that it plans to revive the iconic Celica brand which brought success to the manufacturer through the 1970s, '80s and '90s, winning back-to-back manufacturers' crowns in 1993 and 1994. The car famously guided Carlos Sainz to drivers' titles in 1990 and 1992, with Juha Kankkunen and Didier Auriol going on to win championships in 1993 and 1994 respectively.

The Celica, which will also be piloted by defending world champion Elfyn Evans and Sami Pajari under the Toyota Racing moniker, will go up against a GR Yaris driven by Ott Tanak, Kalle Rovanpera and Takamoto Katsuta as part of Toyota's bold new strategy. It will see Toyota split its expanded six-car WRC effort into two distinct teams, running two models of car that will be identical underneath the body shell.

Solberg only learned that he will be driving the Celica at the launch but is excited to be part of such a legacy brand in the WRC, and one that has a family connection given his father made his WRC debut in 1998 driving a Celica.

"It's awesome. I think it's a cool angle. It's a different way of doing it, which I think is unique for any sport," Solberg told Motorsport.com when asked about Toyota's 2027 strategy.

"I think having the opportunity to have a lot of drivers with different cars, you can have more marketing, you can market in different ways. The Celica coming back as a historic legacy brand, I think it's cool for us young drivers to be in a car like that. It's a little bit of history. So I think the angle is pretty awesome from a marketing point of view and myself, Elfyn and Sami to be driving under Toyota Racing is pretty cool.

"It's going to be a crazy rivalry between all the drivers, some part time and some full time. But I think the rivalry is going to be crazy and really fun."

Solberg ready to heal the hurt of agonising title defeat

Oliver Solberg, Elfyn Evans, Sami Pajari

While the focus is fully on 2027, Solberg admits that losing this year's title by running off the road in the final stage of the season in Sardinia still stings.

However, on reflection of his maiden year in Rally1, he is ultimately proud and glad to have played a part in raising the profile of the championship following the dramatic title showdown climax that went viral on social media.

"I'm okay now," he said. "I'm great to be honest. For sure, it still hurts a little bit in my heart, but I mean, I think when you take a step back and look at it all and experience it all afterwards, you're just very proud of the whole season, of the rollercoaster we had and still be able to fight at the end like that, and never giving up and really trying my very best and showing my potential.

"I think we speak about 150 metres here, it's not far away from being world champion. But again, I didn't give away my championship there. I probably gave it away earlier in the year. I can't explain why it happened in the last corner there, it just happened. It took me by surprise, like everyone else. That's why I also think I can move on quicker, and all the support from the world, all the messages, the hype, everything has just been amazing. So I really think it's been a great outcome.

"I think this is what sport is about. This is what builds every sport up to be something great, and I think we need these stories, these unique moments, and then we need someone to show it also, kick it up in the world. I think what was great is all these messages I received around the world from different athletes in motorsport and not motorsport, everyone's like, 'wow, what is rallying? What is this? This was the craziest thing we've ever seen.'

"I think you need to use it [the moment] to the maximum now, especially now when you see the investment Toyota is putting in for the future. Everyone needs to work together now to really bring the sport to the next level."

Looking ahead to the 2027 season, Solberg says he is even more hungry to reach the pinnacle of rallying by claiming the WRC title.

"The hunger is always there. The passion is always there," he added. "I didn't give up to the end so the belief is there and that's the most important, especially now with all the experience you build through a year, all the learning you've had through a year, through the good and the low moments, so I think the potential and the belief is definitely there for next year to build on something."

articles.title: Oregon 'expected' to be without starting RB vs Ohio State
articles.summary: The Oregon Ducks are "expected" to without starting running back Jordon Davison in their game against the Ohio State Buckeyes.
articles.body:
Every game is a must-win for the Oregon Ducks at this point of the season, and they will be without one of their top players on Saturday against the Ohio State Buckeyes .

According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, starting running back Jordon Davison is expected to miss the game with a "lower extremity injury." The good news is that it is not expected to be a long-term injury, with Zenitz saying he is essentially week-to-week.

Davison is Oregon 's leading rusher, with 91 carries for 439 yards and seven touchdowns. Dierre Hill Jr. has been Oregon's No. 2 running back all year, carrying the ball 83 times for 399 yards and three touchdowns. However, he was limited to just four carries in last week's win over the Northwestern Wildcats, and they relied on Brandon Smith.

The freshman had the best game of his young career, carrying the ball eight times for 82 yards and a touchdown in his fourth appearance of the season. Oregon will release its initial availability report on Wednesday night, providing more clarity on Davison and Hill.

articles.title: Sophomore point guard emerging as silver lining for Nets amid disappointing 1-6 start
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets haven’t had much to write home about during their 1-6 start. Sophomore point guard Nolan Traore has emerged as a silver lining for the rebu...
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets haven't had much to write home about during their 1-6 start. Sophomore point guard Nolan Traore has emerged as a silver lining for the rebuilding squad amid its early struggles.

After an underwhelming rookie campaign, Traore has looked like an NBA point guard while stepping into a starting role. The 20-year-old has averaged 14.8 points on 27-of-53 (50.9 percent) shooting from the field and 12-of-24 (50.0 percent) from three, with 4.0 assists and 2.0 turnovers per game over his last five outings.

"I think number one is development, and you can see it with the amount of games [Nolan] played last year, but also development through the summer and how he worked on his body and then the confidence that he's playing with," said head coach Jordi Fernandez. "And you could see it [against the Indiana Pacers] that he was playing really hard to start and shots didn't fall for anybody, but then he stayed with it, and he made four huge threes that helped us win the game. At the same time, he was touching the paint, spraying the ball, doing all the right things. So his growth has been great, but again, it comes with development through playing games, which I think I've already said: the best coach in the world is playing real games, and it's better to play competitive games and then all the hard work that you put in the summer [pays off]."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Traore's dramatic improvement as a catch-and-shoot three-point shooter has driven much of his scoring production. After shooting 31.8 percent from three as a rookie, the 6-foot-4 guard has shot 12-of-24 (50.0 percent) this season, with all of his makes coming off the catch.

Traore drained four second-half threes against the Pacers on Sunday to lift the Nets to their first win. He shot 5-of-6 from three during Monday's 103-90 loss to the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

Nolan Traore off to promising start to sophomore campaign as Nets' starting point guard

The former No. 19 pick said at Media Day that improving his shooting form was a primary offseason focus.

"I worked a lot on [my shot], and I feel good now. I changed a few things… I won't have a completely different shot from last year. It was more focused on just having the same form every time," Traore said.

Traore's three-point shooting could become a deadly complement to his blazing speed, especially if he becomes comfortable shooting off the dribble. The French floor general has also taken strides as an interior scorer, a main weakness of his game as a rookie.

Traore touched the paint at a high rate last season. However, he converted just 44.6 percent of his shots at the rim, ranking dead-last among 230 players with at least 130 attempts, per Synergy. The 6-foot-4 guard has improved to 47.8 percent early this season, converting 11-of-23 rim attempts. He's also posted a 2.0 assist-to-turnover ratio, up from 1.65 last season.

"For me, it was a lot of the physical aspect," Traore said at media day about his offseason training. "I spent a lot of time in the gym during the summer. That was the main focus. It's going to help me [on the court] for sure. It was just a good thing for me."

With rookie No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. on a minutes restriction, Traore has started the Nets' last four games. Whether Brown eventually enters the starting lineup or not, Fernandez has said Traore will play a critical role as one of the team's two featured point guards.

The Nets coach said Traore has worked hard to develop his voice on the court and in the locker room.

"I think that I can speak for that because when you're a foreigner, there is a language barrier," Fernandez said. "When I came here, my English was very broken, and you have to communicate to play this game, whether you're a coach or a player, especially in the point guard position. So [Nolan's] done a great job because of his willingness to try and do it with confidence, and it takes time. And I think right now, you see those 365 days or more, how much better he's gotten. It's because he's put time into it, and we're going to keep having an accent, but I think people understand what we're saying."

Egor Demin drove the limited optimism around the Nets' 2025 draft class last season. Three of the team's NBA-record five first-round picks from 2025 — Drake Powell, Danny Wolf and Ben Saraf — are out of the rotation to start this season.

Traore developing into a reliable rotation piece would go a long way towards improving the perception of the Nets' biggest draft class in franchise history.

articles.title: Charles Leclerc to miss Brazilian GP media duties after welcoming first child
articles.summary: Leclerc will miss his media duties in Brazil after becoming a father, delaying his response to Hamilton’s criticism following their Mexico Grand Prix clash.
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc will not take part in media commitments ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix after celebrating the birth of his first child.

The Monegasque driver announced on Instagram that his wife Alexandra gave birth to their daughter Bianca on Tuesday.

Although Leclerc was originally set to take questions from reporters on Thursday, he has been granted extra time to remain at home with his family in Monaco.

The 29-year-old's absence means he will not immediately address criticism from team-mate Lewis Hamilton following their clash at the Mexico Grand Prix last weekend.

Hamilton accused Leclerc of working against him when attempting an opening-lap overtake on the British driver while the pair were in front, enabling Max Verstappen to take the victory.

"We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure," said Hamilton.

"We don't have rules of engagement and, whether or not that will change anything from Charles' side, I don't know. Something needs to change for sure.

"I think it's a mentality thing. It's like, 'Do or die. Either I win or none of us do', and it shouldn't be that."

The situation caused frustration for Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur , who remarked to Sky Sports: "I think it's just a matter of respect. Honestly, it's difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this."

Despite the in-fighting and confusion over priorities, Ferrari still have a good chance at claiming second in both the drivers' and constructors' championship.

Lewis Hamilton currently sits in third on 259 points, just two points behind a resurgent Max Verstappen and Leclerc is in fifth on 245 points, behind his teammate and George Russell - but only 16 points separate the remainder of the top five once the newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli is removed from the equation.

Second in the constructors' championship is more than likely tied up for the Scuderia as they hold a commanding 122 point lead over Red Bull but also sit 126 points back from the leaders Mercedes.

articles.title: Palmer should have been sent off for Fernandes barge - panel
articles.summary: Cole Palmer should have received a straight red card for violent conduct in Chelsea's 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur, the Premier League Key Match Incidents (...
articles.body:
Cole Palmer should have received a straight red card for violent conduct in Chelsea's 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur, the Premier League Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has ruled.

The England international was cautioned by referee Chris Kavanagh in the 70th minute after barging into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

Palmer did so with such force that it caused the Portugal international's head to snap back.

The KMI Panel voted 3:2 that Kavanagh should have shown a red card on the field.

However, the KMI Panel unanimously supported the decision of the VAR, John Brooks, not to intervene.

The majority of the five members of the KMI Panel felt it was "clear contact to the head as well as unnecessary, dangerous and made with excessive force".

Two panellists viewed the action as "aggressive with no excessive force", supporting the booking.

Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a foul on Jan Paul van Hecke, which the KMI Panel supported 4:1.

The midfielder received a one-match ban for his dismissal, missing the Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool.

Had he been sent off for violent conduct, he would also have been suspended for Saturday's 2-0 victory over Manchester United, in which he scored a penalty, and this weekend's trip to Sunderland.

The KMI Panel also voted 3:2 that Dominic Solanke should have been awarded an 85th minute penalty for a foul by Moises Caicedo, but with a 3:2 vote supporting no VAR intervention.

The majority felt that "Caicedo was persistently holding Solanke whilst facing away from the ball and impacting the ability of the opponent to progress".

articles.title: Javi Leal se rinde a Lebrón: "No he visto a nadie hacer lo que él hace"
articles.standfirst: El revés andaluz atiende a MARCA en Doha
articles.summary: El revés andaluz atiende a MARCA en Doha
articles.body: La vida da muchas vueltas y eso bien lo sabe Javi Leal (El Puerto de Santa María, 2003). El revés andaluz no formaba parte de la convocatoria de Juanjo Gutiérrez para el Mundial de pádel celebrado esta semana en Qatar. Tras ganar un torneo, hizo el gesto del teléfono a cámara para el seleccionador, luego se filtraron unos audios de este último gastándole una broma y, días después, el gaditano está defendiendo a España con el objetivo de salir campeón. Debido a la baja de Ale Galán, Juanjo Gutiérrez llamó a Leal para entrar en su lugar. Un sustituto de garantías (número 17 del ranking FIP) para intentar batir a Argentina en una hipotética final. Javi, que ya ha vestido la camiseta de ‘La Roja’ en categorías inferiores y torneos de menor calibre como el Europeo, atiende a MARCA para contar cómo han sido estos días tan frenéticos, la convivencia dentro de la concentración y sus sensaciones de cara a este Mundial. Pregunta: Antes de nada, ¿cómo está, Javi? Respuesta: La verdad es que estoy súper contento. He debutado con la selección con Mike Yanguas y la verdad es que no puedo estar más contento. No he estado nervioso, gracias al gran equipo que tenemos. Me han ayudado bastante a entrar relajado y jugar tranquilo. Estoy muy contento. P: ¿Cómo se tomó un poco la noticia de que, de repente, sí pasaba a estar dentro del equipo? R: Bueno, al final es raro, porque se lesiona un compañero. A Galán lo aprecio mucho. Yo cuando me vine a Madrid me ayudó bastante y al final que se lesione no es agradable. Pero bueno, dentro de lo malo me lo tomé bien, porque iba a representar a mi país. Solo queda mandarle mucha fuerza a Ale y que se recupere lo antes posible. P: ¿Cómo se lo comunicaron? ¿Fue de alguna forma en especial? ¿Le llamó Juanjo? R: Sí, me llamó Juanjo el viernes por la mañana. Estaba dormido además, y cuando me desperté tenía dos o tres llamadas perdidas de él. Me dijo: “Mira, Javi, que vas a venir a la selección, Ale no puede venir". Y eso fue lo que me comunicó. P: Con Juanjo también se exageró todo mucho en redes sociales con los audios, el gesto… R: Yo con Juanjo me llevo muy bien. Si lo que hicimos fue todo coña. Lo que pasa es que hay gente que no lo quiere interpretar así o que no sabe interpretarlo de esa manera. Nosotros con Juanjo tenemos buena relación, tanto Fran como yo. Ahora aquí en el Mundial estoy mucho tiempo con él, estamos haciendo bromas. Después de que salieran todos los mensajes de que nos pedía dinero, que no nos pedía dinero, era en plan chiste, pero bueno, yo estaba con él y todo perfecto. Lo veo en cada torneo, me saludo con él, me he ido a comer con él… No tenemos ningún problema. P: ¿Cómo de bien le viene a la selección un carácter como el de Juanjo? Porque cuando se tiene que poner serio, lo hemos visto, se pone serio, pero también es una persona bromista, graciosa, cercano con los jugadores… R: El 90% es gracia. Está todo el rato haciendo chistes y demás. Sí, le viene bien. Sabe en qué momento hacer la broma, sabe en qué momento estar serio, y para mí a la selección le viene bastante bien. Más que nada porque somos ocho “cafres” a cada cual más loco. Entonces le viene bastante bien. Que desde aquí le quiero agradecer al ‘Lobo’ también porque la verdad es que me está ayudando muchísimo. La manera que tiene de actuar conmigo… Por ejemplo, antes de jugar el ‘Lobo’ ha estado hablando conmigo: "Mira, Javi, juega tranquilo, tranquilízate, disfruta". La relación entre todos es muy buena. P: Ha vestido la camiseta de España en otras ocasiones. ¿Le resta eso presión o en un Mundial es diferente? R: No he tenido presión, pero cuando nos han roto en el segundo set, que nos han hecho el break, ahí un poquito de nervio te sale, porque es normal. Esta camiseta pesa, cuando te metes ahí en la pista, pesa. Pero bueno, al final es normal. P: ¿Quién está siendo un poco el líder espiritual del equipo? R: Lebrón, 100%. P: ¿Pero por qué? R: Porque está con todo. Ayer Mike estaba regulín y saltó el ‘Lobo’ y quiso ayudarlo. Lo que le he dicho antes, a mí hoy me ha ayudado muchísimo. Aimar, ayer lo estaba intentando tranquilizar en medio del partido... Para mí está siendo el ‘Lobo’, 100%. P: ¿Cómo está siendo la convivencia? R: Compartimos momentos de habitaciones. Yo tengo la PlayStation aquí y Aimar también, así que jugamos juntos. Aunque haya hecho el gestito del teléfono, lo voy a aclarar aquí, ya que estamos, yo no fui en ningún momento a por Aimar, ni por Juanjo. No fui a por nadie. Fue un gesto que hicimos entre nosotros dos y fin. Yo con Aimar muy bien, con Jon muy bien… Aimar cuando se enteró de que entraba a la selección me escribió. Quería aclararlo. P: Entra por Galán, sustituto de sobra de garantías, pero al final Galán es Galán. ¿Usted cree que nos resta un poco de favoritismo a España de cara a jugar contra Argentina? R: Para mí no nos resta. O sea, sí que es verdad que no soy Galán, porque es una realidad. Galán ha sido el número uno y ahora está siendo el número dos y no se baja de las finales. Pero bueno, yo voy a intentar aportar todo lo que pueda al equipo, voy a intentar hacerlo lo mejor posible y esperemos ganar. P: ¿Se ve jugando la final? R: Tenemos ocho jugadores, cuatro reveses, puedes jugar a cualquiera. De los cuatro, todos tenemos el nivel y Juanjo es el que decide. P: ¿Y un tercer partido? R: Sinceramente, a mí me gustaría jugarlo, porque a mí me gusta jugar en esos momentos y la verdad que... a mí me gustaría, pero es lo que le digo, Juanjo es el que decide y lo que ponga estará perfecto. P: Quizás hay algunos que se parecen más a Fran, que es su compañero habitual, hay otros que se parecen menos… ¿Con qué compañero se está viendo usted que le está gustando compartir pista? ¿Con el Lobo, con Arturo…? R: Mira, esta mañana hemos entrenado y es que yo tengo una debilidad con el ‘Lobo’. No porque sea del Puerto, ojo. Me conoce desde que tengo siete años. Pero no, a mí el ‘Lobo’ me encanta. Yo siempre he dicho que el ‘Lobo’ para mí es mi jugador favorito. Yo no he visto a alguien hacer lo que hace ese hombre con una pelota. De derecha, de revés… En todos lados le juega. Una pasada.

articles.title: Kendrick Perkins gives Luka Doncic the Kobe Bryant treatment amid ridiculous start
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic has had a phenomenal start to the season, and Kendrick Perkins has drawn comparisons to Kobe Bryant. On the latest editio...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic has had a phenomenal start to the season, and Kendrick Perkins has drawn comparisons to Kobe Bryant. On the latest edition of the Road Trippin' podcast, Perkins put Doncic's play and mentality into perspective.

Perkins said Doncic's mentality makes him the closest thing to Kobe Bryant among the league's young stars.

"Luka is the closest thing to Kobe Bryant that we've seen out of all the young guys that are coming up. He don't give a damn, honestly, what his teammates feel about him when they're on the floor. It's not a shot that he don't love or don't think that he can't make, and he can make them."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

He said that fearlessness is essential for handling the pressure of playing in a big market like Los Angeles.

"On top of that, you have to have the kahunas, the onions, to be able to perform and not give a damn on the stage like LA. There's certain cities that come with so much pressure, and you gotta have the I-don't-give-up attitude. He has that."

Perkins added that Doncic isn't intimidated by any defender, no matter how elite.

"He don't give a damn who's in front of him. It could be Giannis, it could be Bam, it could be the best wing defender in the league. Luka is going to tear your a** up. He's the closest thing to Kobe, not game-wise, mentality-wise, out of all the young guys that I done seen."

He also predicted Doncic's scoring pace will hold up through the season.

"I don't think it's slowing down anytime soon. I think we're gonna look up come March and April, and he's still gonna be averaging over that 34 to 35 points a night."

Luka Doncic has started the year on a significant scoring tear. To start the season, he's averaging 38.3 points, 8.1 assists, 8 rebounds, with 1.9 steals while shooting 42.7% from the three-point range.

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck Writes Letter to Jets Fans, Explains Reasons for Trade Request After Devils Move
articles.summary: New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck pointed toward "challenging circumstances involving my family" when explaining why he wanted to leave Winnipeg in an Instagram post Wednesday directed toward Jets fans.
articles.body:
New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck pointed toward "challenging circumstances involving my family" when explaining why he wanted to leave Winnipeg in an Instagram post Wednesday directed toward Jets fans.

"I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career. I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision," Hellebuyck wrote.

"There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family. After a lot of thought and discussion, we ultimately felt that making a change was the best thing for our family. We've chosen to keep those personal circumstances private, and I hope people can respect that."

Hellebuyck confirmed in August he had requested a trade from the Jets before declining to report to training camp. The Jets suspended him for the first month of the season before trading him Oct. 24 to the Devils.

articles.summary: The Falcons held a walkthrough upon arriving in Madrid on Wednesday and they release their estimated practice report for the day after that session came to a...
articles.body:
The Falcons held a walkthrough upon arriving in Madrid on Wednesday and they release their estimated practice report for the day after that session came to an end.

Linebacker James Pearce took part in the walkthrough and was listed as a full participant as he moves toward making his 2026 debut. Pearce missed the first eight games while serving a Personal Conduct Policy suspension related to a domestic violence incident earlier this year.

Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was the only player listed as out of practice. The Falcons announced earlier this week that Branch will not play against the Bengals on Sunday. Defensive end Samson Ebukam was also ruled out before being placed on injured reserve on Tuesday.

Linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) were listed as limited participants. Defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring), wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were listed as full participants.
